analysis.title: Americas Technology: Semiconductors: SIA data shows mostly below-seasonal trends in September following a strong August
key_insights: Shipments of integrated circuit units ex. memory rose ~13% M/M in September, worse than typical seasonality, per SIA data.

Most segments shipped below seasonal levels in September, but NAND and MCU units rose more than seasonal M/M. GS ties this to its constructive view on NAND's role in AI inference and the ongoing industrial recovery.
Total semiconductor shipments are tracking ~13% above long-term demand on a three-month moving average, versus ~10% above trend in August.
Analog units are running ~13% above trend (13.3% vs 11.0% in August), consistent with constructive company commentary on analog demand.
IC units ex. memory were 11.5% above trend versus 9.3% above in August.
MCU units were 18.7% below trend, an improvement from 20.9% below trend in August. MCU units rose ~21.7% M/M, better than the historical median.

DRAM revenue rose 17% M/M, far better than typical seasonality, while DRAM units rose only 3% M/M, worse than seasonal. NAND revenue rose 7% M/M, slightly worse than seasonal, while NAND units rose 8% M/M, better than seasonal.

GS expects shipments to stabilize above trend in the medium term, given four years of below-trend shipments and improving management commentary on datacenter, aerospace and defense, and industrial demand.
GS prefers Microchip, NXP and Analog Devices, because they shipped furthest below trend in the downturn and have more exposure to end markets expected to lead the analog recovery.
